mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 2% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of instances following a triggered INDPRO decline, indicating the market is shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, increasing by more than 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period, signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises by > 5 points during the signal period, indicating the labor market weakening is not impacting consumer spending attitudes.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that will slow economic growth and compress S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Real GDP growth accelerates by > 1% QoQ during the signal period, indicating the economy is resisting the restrictive monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The NAHB Housing Market Index rises by > 5 points during the signal period, indicating homebuilder sentiment is improving despite the drop in housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows by more than 100,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months, it signals a rapidly weakening labor market that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth slows by > 100k jobs/mo for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims decline by > 10% during the signal period, indicating the labor market is not as weak as the payroll growth suggests.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales growth accelerates by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals a surge in consumer demand that will boost corporate revenues and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer sentiment (University of Michigan index) declines by > 5 points during the signal period, indicating the retail sales surge may not be sustainable.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate exceeds 4%, it signals an overheating economy that will prompt the Fed to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed cuts interest rates during the signal period, indicating they are prioritizing growth over fighting inflation.
